findings.title: Monitor context returns the raw config, not the copy with the readable schedule_type
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config into `config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its display value (e.g. "crontab" or "interval"). The returned dict then uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the local `config`, so the conversion is computed and thrown away. As a result, the `monitor` context on every incident occurrence event shows the raw integer `schedule_type` rather than the readable label. This bug existed before, but the function is being moved into a new module, so this is a good time to change it to return `config`.

findings.title: `get_failure_reason` docstring examples don't match the strings it produces
findings.body: The docstring gives examples like "3 missed check-ins detected", "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". The code actually produces "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected" for mixed statuses: it never says "were" and never adds a per-status "check-in". For a single failure it produces "An error/A missed/A timeout check-in was detected", never "A failed check-in". The docstring also misspells "human readable" as "humam readible". Since the function now lives in its own module and will be extended, the documented contract should match the real output.
